tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
schema.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
If the user hasn't said what the model is for (a game asset, a character to rig, a render, a 3D print, AR), ask before you pick models (Rule 4). A game asset or a face-count budget means smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2 with target_polycount), also on meshy_text_to_3d; never a meshy-7.1 model remeshed down.
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one; on meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d also the texture_model, suggesting a pair from "Choosing Models" below), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k"); retexture meshy-n1 10 (2K only) |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | 20 (texture_model meshy-7 only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

texture_model never changes the price; 4K/8K need the meshy-7 or meshy-6 texture model. Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Choosing Models (meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d)
Choose models by project (geometry ai_model + texture_model):
- Detailed hero asset, product render, cinematic prop: meshy-7.1 + meshy-7 (PBR, up to 8K)
- Game character to rig and animate: meshy-t2.5 (smart topology, set target_polycount) + meshy-n1
- Many props for a game scene, or user-generated content: meshy-t2 (smart topology) + meshy-n1
- A real object from 2 to 4 photos: meshy-7.1 on Multi-Image to 3D + meshy-7
- A model to 3D print: meshy-7.1 + none, or meshy-7 to print in color
- Many drafts at a low cost: meshy-6-lite + meshy-6-lite
More: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/models
Omit texture_model for the geometry's default; "none" is should_texture false; smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2) is single-image only. A texture model refuses options it cannot do (e.g. meshy-n1: no texture_prompt, enable_pbr or 4K); the tool says so before any charge.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the ta… [truncated]

# Jam dev log (goal: the Glass Box prize for the best dev log)

Everything any agent or person does on the project must be recorded here. If it is not in the dev log, it did not happen as far as the judges are concerned.

**Language:** the Official Rules (7(i)) require every part of the submission in English, and that includes the published dev log. Write `days/*.md`, `media/` captions and `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` in English. Raw logs (`raw/`) and the team's prompts to agents can be in any language. When a day entry quotes a prompt written in Spanish, include the original and an English translation.

## Layout

```
Devlog/
  README.md                  this file (the rules)
  TEMPLATE_DAY.md            template for the daily entry
  PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md     what was prepared BEFORE Nov 12 (the jam requires declaring it)
  PREJAM_PREP.md             full pre-jam log: timeline, tests, tools evaluated, rules read
  raw/<MACHINE>/             raw automatic logs (NEVER published as they are)
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/claude-<session>.jsonl      every Claude Code event (hook)
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/transcripts/<session>.jsonl full transcript of each session
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents.jsonl                every run of an external agent
    <YYYY-MM-DD>/agents/<run>/               prompt, full output and diffstat of that run
    unreal/<log>.jsonl                       agent actions inside the Editor (MCP, Assistant, Canvas)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>_DRAFT.md                 automatic draft (already redacted)
  days/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md                       final entry for the day, written by a person (in English)
  media/<YYYY-MM-DD>/                        screenshots, gifs and clips of the day
```

## Rules for everyone (people and agents)

1. **Claude Code** is logged automatically by the **user-level** hooks that `Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1` installs on each machine. They log every session opened in the jam root or any subfolder (the root is the folder that contains `Devlog/.jamroot`). Do not disable them and do not delete `.jamroot`.
2. **Any other agent** (Codex, cursor-agent, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Gemini, generation scripts) is ALWAYS launched with:
   `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent <name> -Model <model> -PromptFile <prompt.md> -Purpose "<what for>" -Command '<command>'`
   - Use `-Shell cmd` if the command contains `< file`.
   - That is what records it. An agent launched by hand leaves no record.
   - **Cursor** (the art LAPTOP, which has no repo) is logged by user-level Cursor hooks instead: `Tools/Devlog/Install-CursorHooks.ps1` installs `cursor-devlog-hook.ps1`, which writes `C:\JamLog\raw\<MACHINE>\<date>\cursor-<conversation>.jsonl` (plus transcripts). `Register-LaptopDevlogTasks.ps1` copies that folder every 10 minutes to `Incoming\LAPTOP\_devlog_raw` on CENTRAL, and CENTRAL's `JamDevlogImport` task (`Import-RemoteDevlog.ps1`) moves it into `Devlog/raw/`, where `New-DevlogDay.ps1` reads it. The same kit runs on ASSETS (destination `Incoming\ASSETS\_devlog_raw`).
   - **Codex chats** (desktop app, IDE extension or interactive CLI, i.e. anything not launched through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`) on machines without the repo: before each sync, `Collect-CodexSessions.ps1` copies the session files Codex keeps in `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\sessions` (full prompts, replies and tool calls) into `C:\JamLog\raw\<MACHINE>\<date>\codex-*.jsonl`. `New-DevlogDay.ps1` reads those too.
   - **Cursor transcripts:** `Collect-CursorTranscripts.ps1` also copies the full agent transcripts Cursor keeps in `%USERPROFILE%.cursorprojects*gent-transcripts`, so chats from before the hook was installed are not lost. The draft takes Cursor prompts from the transcript whenever there is one (it is complete; the hook missed some prompts before the mutex fix).
   - **Claude Code and Gemini CLI** on machines without the repo: `Collect-OtherAgents.ps1` copies their session files (`%USERPROFILE%.claudeprojects`, `%USERPROFILE%.gemini	mp`). OpenCode keeps its sessions in a SQLite database, so it is always launched through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`; on ASSETS the sync also sends that repo's `Devlogaw` (`-ExtraSource`).
   - **Size:** every collector strips base64 images (screenshots, renders) from the copies (`JamLogCopy.ps1`): one Codex session on ASSETS went from 110 MB to 4.2 MB with every message and tool call intact. `Import-RemoteDevlog.ps1` refuses files over 50 MB and logs them, because `Devlog/raw` goes to GitHub, which rejects files over 100 MB.
   - On CENTRAL, Codex and OpenCode always run through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`, so this collection is only needed on machines without the repo.
3. **Prompts as files:** external agents get their prompt in a `.md` under `Prompts/`, never typed loose in the terminal.
4. **Web or desktop tools** (Fab, cloud Canvas, audio or image generators, Blender by hand): in the day entry, write down the tool, the prompt, the result and the final asset, and save a screenshot in `media/`.
5. **Unreal Editor:** always close it with `Tools/Jam/Stop-EditorMcp.ps1`, which closes open asset editors first (an open animation editor crashes the Editor on exit) and collects the log. If it was closed some other way, or before deleting `Saved/`, run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Collect-UnrealAgentLog.ps1 -ProjectDir <folder of the .uproject>`.
6. **`JAM_MACHINE` variable:** each machine sets its own (`CENTRAL`, `ASSETS`…) so we know where each thing happened:
   `setx JAM_MACHINE CENTRAL`
7. **Small, frequent commits** with clear messages: the daily draft lists them. Commit `Devlog/raw/` too (the repo is private). Epic may ask for the version control history.
8. **End of day:** run `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/New-DevlogDay.ps1 -Date <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Then a person writes `days/<date>.md` from `TEMPLATE_DAY.md`, starting from the draft.
9. **Publish:** only `days/*.md`, `media/`, `PRE_JAM_DECLARATION.md` and `PREJAM_PREP.md`. Raw logs may contain keys or emails: the draft is already redacted, but check it before publishing. The dev log link goes in the submission, **before the deadline**.
10. **Times in UTC.** The jam ends on Nov 15 at 20:59 EST, which is **01:59 UTC on Nov 16**.

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
If the user hasn't said what the model is for (a game asset, a character to rig, a render, a 3D print, AR), ask before you pick models (Rule 4). A game asset or a face-count budget means smart topology (meshy-t2.5 / meshy-t2 with target_polycount), also on meshy_text_to_3d; never a meshy-7.1 model remeshed down.
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one; on meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d also the texture_model, suggesting a pair from "Choosing Models" below), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

- Game character to rig and animate: meshy-t2.5 (smart topology, set target_polycount) + meshy-n1
- Many props for a game scene, or user-generated content: meshy-t2 (smart topology) + meshy-n1
- A real object from 2 to 4 photos: meshy-7.1 on Multi-Image to 3D + meshy-7
- A model to 3D print: meshy-7.1 + none, or meshy-7 to print in color
- Many drafts at a low cost: meshy-6-lite + meshy-6-lite
More: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/models

# Game Design Document (working draft)

> Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
> Status: **v0.43, 2026-11-13** — owner's vision plus thirteen rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Implementation is delegated as `CLAUDE.md` says ("Implementador").
> Project code name: **Glyphbound** (provisional; the game title is still TBD). Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.

## Changelog
- v0.43 (2026-11-13): owner: **the weapon enchant's element is chosen in its QTE**, always in the same places (never shuffled): a first step shows fire (A / Square), lightning (W / Triangle) and ice (D / Circle); the key picks it, then the usual key sequence and gesture follow. Also from the owner the same day: menus play a transition when their look changes, every skill point asks for confirmation, and the weapon tree is a hub with gun pages (v0.39 to v0.42).
- v0.42 (2026-11-13): owner chose three perk changes the architect proposed from the balance table: the pistol's Steady Grip becomes **Quick Draw** (aim 20% faster and move 10% faster while aiming, per rank), the shotgun's Steady Grip becomes **Extended Tube** (more shells), and the rifle gets **Extended Mag** (+5 rounds per magazine per rank). Measuring them showed that a bigger magazine also carries more ammo (spare magazines hold the bigger magazine; the shotgun's reserve is magazines x tube size), so the architect set Extended Tube to **+1 shell per rank** instead of the +2 shown to the owner: +2 doubled the shells carried, twice any other perk. Details in §18 "Weapon tree".
- v0.41 (2026-11-13): owner: **Marksman, Precision Recovery and Arcane Conduit are general again, as at first** (they work on every gun, Marksman also on the staff and the sword) and sit on the weapon hub with Heavy Rounds; Deadeye stays next to Marksman (they stack, as before); Tight Choke stays. The architect measured every weapon perk with the balance tool (new table "what one point buys") and tuned the new per-gun perks to the existing ones: **Rapid Reload -15% per rank** on each gun (was -10% on all guns at once), **Tight Choke -15%** per rank. Arcane Conduit needs only Heavy Rounds now. Details in §18 "Weapon tree".
- v0.40 (2026-11-13): owner chose **perks per gun**: each gun page has its own perks, and the shared ones ("All guns") are gone. Every gun gets its own Quick Trigger, Rapid Reload and Steady Grip; the pistol keeps Deadeye -> Marksman -> Precision Recovery, the rifle Long Shot -> Arcane Conduit (now rifle-only), the shotgun Point Blank -> a new Tight Choke (tighter pellet spread). The weapon tree goes from 36 to 57 points. Side effect found with the balance tool: the old "All" fire-rate and reload perks also sped up the staff and the sword, so the Entity fight grew from about 191 to 214 s; **each Entity phase goes from 8,000 to 7,300 health** (about 193 s again). Details in §18 "Weapon tree" and §19.
- v0.39 (2026-11-13): owner, after playing the package: **the skill trees are two pages** (tabs; Q / E, L1 / L2 / R1), and each page takes its tree's whole look (spells = RPG, weapons = cyberpunk); the other menus both eras share take **the current era's look** (past = RPG, future = cyberpunk) instead of the held item's; I opens the inventory; the spell page gets a calmer, darker background. **The weapon tree becomes a hub with three gun branches, Cyberpunk style:** Heavy Rounds on top, then Pistol, Rifle and Shotgun; choosing one opens that gun's page, with a Back button. Architect, provisional: the nine existing perks are regrouped by theme with their effects unchanged (§18 "Weapon tree").
- v0.38 (2026-11-13): owner, after seeing it in the arena: **no baked explosion on the Fireball's impact**. The Fireball keeps the baked fire in flight; where it lands it shows the shockwave alone, as before. The explosion clip stays in the plugin for whoever wants it later (§18 "Baked fluid effects").
- v0.37 (2026-11-13): owner: a complete rework of the HUD and menus ("it works but it is basic and ugly"), each skin true to its style, Cyberpunk 2077 as the reference for the cyberpunk one. Both skins are built (§13 "As built"): a carved stone, iron and gilt status bar in pixel art with the game's own pixel font, and a red / cyan cyberpunk HUD with cut corners and condensed type; menus, QTE, death screen, toasts, crosshair and damage numbers follow the held item's skin; ten pixel spell icons. Architect, provisional: the inventory follows the held item's skin; death headlines "YOU HAVE FALLEN" and "FLATLINED".
- v0.36 (2026-11-13): owner: **the Fireball uses the baked fire**. In flight it is the baked fire clip instead of its small sprite; where it explodes the baked explosion plays on top of the shockwave (the explosion is the architect's addition, provisional). Sizes and speed are data in `Spells.json` (§18 "Baked fluid effects"). No other spell is changed.
- v0.35 (2026-11-13): a tool for the game's magic effects, the **GBPixelVfx** plugin (owner's idea; the architect built the minimal version): it bakes a realistic Niagara Fluids effect (fire, smoke, explosion) into a pixel-art flipbook in the master palette and plays it in the game as a camera-facing sprite with a real light. Four clips are baked. **None is used by a spell yet: that waits for the owner's OK.** Rules in §3 "The pixel-art look" and §18.
- v0.34 (2026-11-13): the shotgun is in the game with its 3D model, its pump and its shell-by-shell reload (§18 "Reload"): firing stops the reload at once, a tap on an empty gun fires when the first shell lands, the reserve reads "x24 shells". Owner: its energy bar stays on top of the receiver.
- v0.34 (2026-11-13): the Entity's phase 1 as built (2.5x, a 3D floating boss). Owner: its combat is **pending** polish, including **tentacle melee**. Added to §11 and §17.
- v0.33 (2026-11-12): owner, on the shotgun: it loads **shell by shell** (not a magazine swap), and its **forend pumps** after every shot. Its model is a Tripo science-fiction shotgun. Rules and the architect's provisional numbers in §18 "Reload".
- v0.32 (2026-11-12): the pixel-art line is defined: "dark fantasy hi-bit pixel art, 16-bit inspired", from 9 sprites drawn by hand on the LAPTOP (Valki, axe, sword, two shields, four staffs). Rules, master palette and checklist in `Design/VisualStyleGuide.md`, linked from §3.
- v0.31 (2026-11-12): owner picked the Entity's first model (Tripo, variant #26): a metal shell with electronic-light eyes, and hologram tentacles. Phase 1 art in §11; its size is provisional.
- v0.30 (2026-11-12): owner: the pistol's energy bar must match the enchant's duration; the weak-point light lasts half as long.
- v0.29 (2026-11-12): owner, after reading the balance suggestions: Long Shot goes from +0.15x to +0.2x per rank (the rifle perk now matches Point Blank); the free skill reset will not be in the final version.
- v0.28 (2026-11-12): owner asked the architect to balance every number of the game with maths (the skill-tree percentages stay as they are) and to leave no hardcoded value. New §19 "Balance": the method, the enemy templates (swarm, soldier, elite, slow tank, sub-boss, the two Valkyries, the Entity), resistances and weaknesses, the ammo and mana economy, and a budget of 36 skill points. The numbers in §18 are updated. The last gameplay numbers that lived in code moved to the data files. A calculator, `Tools/Balance/balance_model.js`, prints every table from the data. Reviewed by a second model before the first build.
- v0.27 (2026-11-12): owner: the spell tree is reorganized in four columns (fire, lightning, ice, casting) with only two links kept; Precision Recovery costs 2 points per rank. See §18 "Spell tree".
- v0.25 (2026-11-12): owner approved the first real gun model: the pistol replaces its placeholder (§8 "Guns"). Architect, provisional: its glow follows the enchant element and its energy bar shows the enchant time left.
- v0.24 (2026-11-12): owner: the weapon tree is reorganized (Heavy Rounds on top; a handling branch and a precision branch; three weapon specializations on one row) and gets four new perks: Rapid Reload, Precision Recovery, Arcane Conduit, Deadeye. See §18 "Weapon tree".
- v0.23 (2026-11-12): owner: guns are less accurate while the player moves than while standing still.
- v0.22 (2026-11-12): owner's spec: **elemental build-up** (fire, lightning, ice) on every enemy, with three status effects (Ignite, Shock, Frost), per-enemy resistances and reactions, a weak-point bonus for weapon hits, and every number in data. Owner's answers: the old small effects on every hit (burn, the lightning slow, the enchant's chill) are **removed**; the status effect at the full bar is the only elemental effect (the ice floor keeps its zone slow). The elemental sword and the ember staff build up their element too. See §6 "Elemental build-up".
54:At its core this is a **classic first-person RPG plus a classic first-person shooter**. Anything not stated here behaves as players expect from those two genres (magazines and reload, ammo pickups, standard shooter gamepad layout, etc.). This document only lists what is specific to our game.
73:A fast first-person **shooter/RPG hybrid**: the player, a medieval mage, jumps through fixed portals between a **pixel-art medieval past** full of magic and a **3D cyberpunk future** full of guns, on the same map in two times, and wins by **mixing spells and firearms** rather than sticking to one style.
88:- **The player is a medieval mage, so the player is always pixel art, hands included.** In first person, the hands are always pixel art, even when they hold a 3D gun.
92:- **Visual reference:** retro first-person fantasy shooters with modern lighting (the owner's reference: *Wizordum*). Reference only, nothing copied.
165:| **Ice** | Ice shield (**summoned by the spell, then raised by holding the Block key**, like the shield of a first-person RPG; it only protects while raised; cooldown and limits) | Ice wall | Ice floor: slows enemies, light crowd control |
176:- After the challenge the player gets the element's **knowledge** (from a chest, a book or similar) and **unlocks the missing spells of that element** (fire: fire wall + flamethrower; lightning: rune trap + static ball; ice: ice shield + ice floor).
279:- **One armor slot = one full armor.** No separate helmet, arms or chest pieces.
300:## 9. Controls
394:| Staff (magic) | **1990s first-person RPG** |
401:  - **90s RPG skin** (staff, sword): a status bar of carved dark stone along the bottom with a worn iron rim, a gilt trim line and rivets. A raised crest in the middle holds the five spell sockets: gold bezels, the spell's pixel icon, its mana cost, a cooldown shade with the seconds left, a cold shade when there is not enough mana, the key under each. Life and mana are glass tubes with a liquid ramp and the number beside them (a pale trail shows the life just lost; the heart glows under 30 %); dash is a thin gilt tube. The quick-use item sits in a gold socket at the right, with the skill points and a gem. Active effects and the summoned shield are small stone plaques above the bar. The hands stand on the bar, as in the 90s games. Everything is laid out on a grid of whole art pixels (4 screen pixels at 1080p, 3 at 720p) in the master palette of `Design/VisualStyleGuide.md` (obsidian, iron, bone, blood, ice; a gilt ramp made from the wood and bone ramps), with **the game's own 5 x 7 pixel font**, drawn for the game during the jam and baked into gold, bone, blood, ice and ember inks.
424:| 1 (Nov 12) | First-person controller (move, dash, double jump), pixel-art hands, one staff, one gun, one spell with data-driven parameters, mana/health, one portal swapping eras in a test map. Packaged. |
440:- **Rendering of the art rule per object:** pixel-art sprites (player hands, medieval props, enemies, spells) and 3D meshes (guns, cyberpunk world) in the same first-person view.
466:## 18. Provisional rules and numbers picked by the architect (2026-11-12)
470:- **Jumps commit to their direction (owner, 2026-11-12):** like a real jump, the direction cannot be changed in the air (air control 0; the same when walking off a ledge). The direction is chosen at takeoff: the movement keys held at that moment. The second jump can choose a new direction and then commits again. Provisional details (architect): a jump from standing with a direction held leaves at 60% of walking speed at least; the second jump with a direction held leaves at walking speed at least, and with no direction held it keeps the current drift. The dash still works in the air and is not affected.
476:  - **The shotgun's forend pumps after every shot (owner, 2026-11-12).** Provisional (architect): it is only the look; the time between shots stays `FireInterval` (0.8 s) and the pump plays inside it. **As built (v0.34), provisional art values:** it starts back at 22% of the interval, is fully back at 45% and home at 72%; the gun dips 0.5 cm and rolls 1.5° with it and the 2D left hand rides it. From the first-person camera the pump itself is under the gun and hardly seen.
493:- **Enemies and cover (after the first play-test):** enemies walk around obstacles. A melee enemy only starts its attack when it sees the player; a ranged enemy that loses sight stops aiming and moves until it sees the player again. Enemies do not walk off ledges on their own; one that falls out of the map dies without drops.
Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound
Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Enemies
Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Enemies/Entity
Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Enemies/Entity_Preview
Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Materials
Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Weapons
Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Weapons/Pistol
Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Weapons/Rifle
Glyphbound/Content/Glyphbound/Weapons/Shotgun

<#
Smoke-Jam.ps1 - Runs the game by itself (console command "gb.Smoke": a scripted run of the main systems that
takes screenshots and quits) and reports what happened. It is NOT Play In Editor and nobody plays: it only
tells us whether the game starts, the systems run without crashing, and what the screen looks like.
A person still has to play the build.

Usage:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1              # uncooked game with the Editor binaries (-game)
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Packaged    # the packaged build in Glyphbound/Build/Windows
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Only Entity -Offscreen   # only the Entity steps, no window
Output: the SMOKE lines, errors and warnings of our log category, and the list of screenshots.
Exit code: 0 = the script reached "SMOKE DONE" with no error lines and no crash.
#>
param(
    [switch]$Packaged,
    [string]$Only = '',      # filtered run: only the steps whose name starts with this (for example Entity), then quit
    [switch]$Offscreen,        # adds -RenderOffscreen: no window pops up
    [string]$Project = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..\Glyphbound\Glyphbound.uproject'),
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 180,
    [int]$ResX = 1280,        # screenshot size (for example 1920 x 1080 to judge the HUD)
    [int]$ResY = 720
)
$Project = (Resolve-Path $Project).Path
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$stamp = [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('yyyyMMdd-HHmmss')
$smokeCmd = if ($Only) { "gb.Smoke $Only" } else { 'gb.Smoke' }
$common = @('-windowed', "-ResX=$ResX", "-ResY=$ResY", '-unattended', '-nosplash', '-nosound', "-ExecCmds=`"$smokeCmd`"")
if ($Offscreen) { $common += '-RenderOffscreen' }
if ($Packaged) {
    $exe = Join-Path $projDir 'Build\Windows\Glyphbound.exe'
    if (-not (Test-Path $exe)) { Write-Host "No packaged build at $exe"; exit 2 }
    $shotDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Build\Windows\Glyphbound\Saved\Screenshots\Smoke'
    $log = Join-Path $projDir 'Build\Windows\Glyphbound\Saved\Logs\Glyphbound.log'
    $argList = $common
} else {
    $exe = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor.exe'
    $shotDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\Screenshots\Smoke'
    $log = Join-Path $projDir "Saved\Logs\smoke_$stamp.log"
    $argList = @("`"$Project`"", '-game', "-abslog=`"$log`"") + $common
}
if (Test-Path $shotDir) { Remove-Item (Join-Path $shotDir '*.png') -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
$p = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $argList -PassThru
$timedOut = -not $p.WaitForExit($TimeoutSeconds * 1000)
if ($timedOut) {
    # This is the game process, not the Editor: stopping it is safe.
    Write-Host "TIMEOUT after $TimeoutSeconds s: stopping the game process."
    Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Start-Sleep 2
}
$sw.Stop()
if (-not (Test-Path $log)) { Write-Host "No log at $log (exit $($p.ExitCode))"; exit 2 }
$lines = Get-Content $log -Encoding UTF8
$smoke = @($lines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'SMOKE' })
$bad = @($lines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'LogGB: (Error|Warning)|Fatal error|Unhandled Exception|Assertion failed|Ensure condition failed|appError' })
$otherErrors = @($lines | Where-Object { $_ -match ': Error: ' -and $_ -notmatch 'LogGB' })
$smoke | ForEach-Object { ($_ -replace '^\[[^\]]*\]\[[^\]]*\]', '').Trim() }
Write-Host '---- problems in our code (LogGB warnings/errors, asserts, crashes) ----'
if ($bad.Count -eq 0) { Write-Host '(none)' } else { $bad | Select-Object -First 40 | ForEach-Object { ($_ -replace '^\[[^\]]*\]\[[^\]]*\]', '').Trim() } }

---
name: astra-is-gpt-6-astra-codex
description: "Astra" = GPT-6-Astra consulted through the Codex CLI (model id gpt-6-astra); how to launch it in GameJam
metadata:
  type: reference
---

When the owner says "consulta con Astra" (or "Astra 6"), they mean the model **GPT-6-Astra through the Codex CLI**, model id `gpt-6-astra` (listed in `~/.codex/models_cache.json`; the default in `~/.codex/config.toml` is `gpt-6.1-sol`). "En medio" = `-c model_reasoning_effort=medium`.

In GameJam it must go through the logged wrapper, read-only, with the prompt in a file under `Prompts/`:
`powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent codex -Model "gpt-6-astra (medium)" -PromptFile Prompts\x.md -Purpose "..." -Shell cmd -Command "codex exec -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=medium -s read-only -C . - < Prompts\x.md"`
The answer is at the end of `Devlog/raw/CENTRAL/<date>/agents/<run>/output.txt` (after the last line that is just `codex`).

**How to apply:** the owner (2026-11-12) wants Astra consulted BEFORE compiling and running tests, so its notes are folded in and there is only one build. See [[implementer-muse-spark-opencode]].
---
name: sonnet-after-muse-stall
description: Owner twice moved work from Muse Spark to Sonnet after Muse stalled (Entity, then the GBPixelVfx plugin), 2026-11-13
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 6b61be55-c028-489d-bfd0-0cff94e53a29
  modified: 2026-11-13T11:31:21.241Z
---

On 2026-11-13 the owner said "Usa sonnet, no Muse" for the Entity's 3D-presence task, right after a Muse Spark run took over 2 hours (it looped on a content bug it could not fix).

Same day, about 11:05 UTC, on the GBPixelVfx plugin: Muse had stalled a second time (2 h 45 min, 53 runs of the same showcase), and the owner said "puedes pasar a Sonnet si quieres" (permission, not an order).

**Why:** Muse's long runs cost time the jam doesn't have. Both stalls had the same shape: a visual / engine bug it could not diagnose, a wrong theory after a few runs, then dozens of runs defending it.

**How to apply:** for GameJam implementation tasks, a Sonnet subagent (Agent tool, model sonnet; Claude Code hooks log it) is allowed without asking, and preferred after any Muse stall. My interpretation: do not hand Muse a "find out why it does not render" task at all; diagnose it myself with engine facts (render time, bounds, a primitive dump), then give the implementer a bounded fix. Stop a Muse run after about 30 min without progress instead of letting it go for hours. Overrides [[implementer-muse-spark-opencode]] here.
---
name: machine-lock-shared
description: GameJam CENTRAL runs several Claude chats at once; builds/game runs must honor Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c499171-af23-4e77-afe4-86028ce8f216
  modified: 2026-11-13T12:45:40.406Z
---

On CENTRAL several architect chats work on the repo at the same time (seen 2026-11-13: the HUD chat and the GBPixelVfx chat). They share one rule: one build or game run at a time, signalled by `Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock` ("who | what | UTC time"; a lock younger than 45 min means wait). `Tools/Jam/PixelVfx-Jam.ps1` implements the wait; `Build-Jam.ps1` and `Smoke-Jam.ps1` do not, so wrap them yourself.

**Why:** a concurrent `Smoke-Jam.ps1` deletes the other chat's screenshots, and a concurrent build fails with "file in use"; the other chat's half-written edits can also break your build for a few minutes.

**How to apply:** before building or running the game, check the lock and running cl.exe/UnrealEditor processes; take the lock while you run. When other chats have uncommitted edits in shared files (GDD.md, GBDevCommands.cpp, Build.cs), commit only your hunks: stage "HEAD + your change" with `git hash-object -w --stdin` + `git update-index --cacheinfo`, never `git add` their files. See [[commit-changes-always]].
---
name: implementer-muse-spark-opencode
description: "Owner's standing rule that Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor (High) via OpenCode is the default implementer in all projects"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 5df7da57-5bde-40bc-a89f-dccc77a1adf3
  modified: 2026-11-12T05:57:27.065Z
---

Default implementer for this and all projects is Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor at High, run through OpenCode (`opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor#high`).

**Why:** the owner likes it and wants everyone on the team to use it as the implementer. Exceptions are the architect's / person-on-duty's call: the orchestrator making small changes directly, or a task too complex for Muse that goes to Opus or similar.

**How to apply:** delegate implementation to OpenCode by default; keep the exceptions rare and note the reason. In GameJam launch it only via `Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`. Config lives in `C:\GameJam\opencode.jsonc` and the global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. The owner wrote "Haiku" once, read as a typo for High. See [[commit-changes-always]].
---
name: review-with-sol-codex
description: "Global rule: review implemented code with Sol 6.1 (gpt-6.1-sol) at medium through Codex CLI, every Claude Code chat"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 6b61be55-c028-489d-bfd0-0cff94e53a29
  modified: 2026-11-13T04:54:01.193Z
---

Owner, 2026-11-13: "recuerda usar Sol 6.1 medium a través de Codex CLI para revisar el código, eso es una regla global para todos los chats de Claude Code". Also added to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

**Why:** the owner's standing review step; I had verified the Entity work (Muse/Sonnet) only with build/tests/smoke and skipped it.

**How to apply:** after an implementer finishes and before committing, write a review prompt in Prompts/ (e.g. `<task>_review_codex.md`) and run, in GameJam, `powershell -File Tools/Devlog/Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent codex -Model gpt-6.1-sol -Shell cmd -PromptFile <file> -Purpose "..." -Command "codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=medium -s read-only -C . - < <file>"`. Fix or send back its findings. Related: [[astra-is-gpt-6-astra-codex]], [[implementer-muse-spark-opencode]].

input.content:
# Task: ledge climb (mantle) for the player — Glyphbound (UE 5.9, C++)

You are the implementer. The architect (Claude Code) designed this; implement it exactly, in C++, in the project at
`C:\GameJam\Glyphbound` (module `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound`). Read `C:\GameJam\CLAUDE.md` first (rules), but you
do NOT edit `Design/GDD.md` or the dev log: the architect does that.

## What the owner asked (translated from Spanish)
"When the character jumps and ends up at the edge of a structure, it should play the climb animation and climb up
that structure. Also, when the character is right against a block/structure and presses jump, if the jump is high
enough, it should play the climb animation and climb that structure/block instead of jumping."

The game is first person (camera only, no body mesh). The player's hands are 2D pixel-art sprites drawn by the HUD
(`UI/GBHUD.cpp`, `AGBHUD::DrawHands`), guns are 3D models attached to `HeldItemAnchor` under the camera. So the
"climb animation" is a first-person one: camera motion + the pixel hands gripping the ledge + the held item lowered.

## Design (architect, provisional; numbers are data)

### New stats in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/Player.json` "Stats" (add constants in `Core/GBStatNames.h`, `GBStat::`)
| Stat | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| MantleMaxReach | 160 | cm: the highest a ledge top can be above the feet for the hands to reach it |
| MantleMinHeight | 50 | cm: from the ground, a ledge lower than this above the feet is not climbed (it is jumped / stepped) |
| MantleAirMinHeight | 15 | cm: in the air, a ledge top less than this above the feet is not climbed (the player just lands) |
| MantleProbeDistance | 40 | cm: how far in front of the capsule a wall is looked for |
| MantleFacingMinDot | 0.5 | the view's yaw forward must face the wall: dot(forward2D, -wallNormal2D) >= this |
| MantleTopInset | 10 | cm: the capsule ends this far past the ledge edge (its edge, not its centre: centre = edge + radius + inset) |
| MantleBaseDuration | 0.22 | s |
| MantleDurationPerMeter | 0.18 | s per metre of rise (duration = base + per metre * rise / 100) |
| MantleRiseShare | 0.6 | share of the duration spent rising straight up; the rest moves forward onto the top |

Read them with `ReadStat` like every other movement stat (they then work with modifiers and missing-stat warnings).

### Pure logic (new files `Player/GBMantle.h` / `.cpp`, namespace `GBMantle`, no UObject, tested)
```
struct FMantleParams { float MaxReach, MinHeight, AirMinHeight, BaseDuration, DurationPerMeter, RiseShare; };
/** One jump's rise: v^2 / (2 g), g = |GravityZ| * GravityScale (guard g <= 0 -> 0). */
float JumpRise(float JumpZVelocity, float Gravity);
/** From the ground, on a jump press: MinHeight <= LedgeHeight <= JumpRise + MaxReach. */
bool CanMantleFromGround(float LedgeHeight, float JumpRiseCm, const FMantleParams&);
/** In the air: AirMinHeight <= LedgeHeight <= MaxReach. */
bool CanMantleFromAir(float LedgeHeight, const FMantleParams&);
float Duration(float RiseCm, const FMantleParams&);   // >= 0.05 s
/** Actor location along the mantle at Alpha in [0,1]: first (0..RiseShare) straight up from Start to (Start.XY, End.Z)
    with an ease-out, then (RiseShare..1) horizontally to End with a smoothstep. Alpha clamped. Exactly Start at 0, End at 1. */
FVector EvaluatePath(const FVector& Start, const FVector& End, float Alpha, float RiseShare);
/** View pose weights at Alpha (all exactly 0 at Alpha 0 and at Alpha 1):
    ItemLower01: 0 -> 1 over the first 20%, 1 until 75%, 1 -> 0 by 100% (smoothstep each ramp).
    Grip01 (pixel hands on the ledge): 0 -> 1 over 0..15%, 1 until 70%, 1 -> 0 by 90%, 0 after.
```

## What the owner asked (translated from Spanish)
"When the character jumps and ends up at the edge of a structure, it should play the climb animation and climb up
that structure. Also, when the character is right against a block/structure and presses jump, if the jump is high
enough, it should play the climb animation and climb that structure/block instead of jumping."

The game is first person (camera only, no body mesh). The player's hands are 2D pixel-art sprites drawn by the HUD
(`UI/GBHUD.cpp`, `AGBHUD::DrawHands`), guns are 3D models attached to `HeldItemAnchor` under the camera. So the
"climb animation" is a first-person one: camera motion + the pixel hands gripping the ledge + the held item lowered.

## Design (architect, provisional; numbers are data)

### New stats in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/Player.json` "Stats" (add constants in `Core/GBStatNames.h`, `GBStat::`)
| Stat | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| MantleMaxReach | 160 | cm: the highest a ledge top can be above the feet for the hands to reach it |
| MantleMinHeight | 50 | cm: from the ground, a ledge lower than this above the feet is not climbed (it is jumped / stepped) |
| MantleAirMinHeight | 15 | cm: in the air, a ledge top less than this above the feet is not climbed (the player just lands) |
| MantleProbeDistance | 40 | cm: how far in front of the capsule a wall is looked for |
| MantleFacingMinDot | 0.5 | the view's yaw forward must face the wall: dot(forward2D, -wallNormal2D) >= this |
| MantleTopInset | 10 | cm: the capsule ends this far past the ledge edge (its edge, not its centre: centre = edge + radius + inset) |
| MantleBaseDuration | 0.22 | s |
| MantleDurationPerMeter | 0.18 | s per metre of rise (duration = base + per metre * rise / 100) |
| MantleRiseShare | 0.6 | share of the duration spent rising straight up; the rest moves forward onto the top |

Read them with `ReadStat` like every other movement stat (they then work with modifiers and missing-stat warnings).

### Pure logic (new files `Player/GBMantle.h` / `.cpp`, namespace `GBMantle`, no UObject, tested)
```
struct FMantleParams { float MaxReach, MinHeight, AirMinHeight, BaseDuration, DurationPerMeter, RiseShare; };
/** One jump's rise: v^2 / (2 g), g = |GravityZ| * GravityScale (guard g <= 0 -> 0). */
float JumpRise(float JumpZVelocity, float Gravity);
/** From the ground, on a jump press: MinHeight <= LedgeHeight <= JumpRise + MaxReach. */
bool CanMantleFromGround(float LedgeHeight, float JumpRiseCm, const FMantleParams&);
/** In the air: AirMinHeight <= LedgeHeight <= MaxReach. */
bool CanMantleFromAir(float LedgeHeight, const FMantleParams&);
float Duration(float RiseCm, const FMantleParams&);   // >= 0.05 s
/** Actor location along the mantle at Alpha in [0,1]: first (0..RiseShare) straight up from Start to (Start.XY, End.Z)
    with an ease-out, then (RiseShare..1) horizontally to End with a smoothstep. Alpha clamped. Exactly Start at 0, End at 1. */
FVector EvaluatePath(const FVector& Start, const FVector& End, float Alpha, float RiseShare);
/** View pose weights at Alpha (all exactly 0 at Alpha 0 and at Alpha 1):
    ItemLower01: 0 -> 1 over the first 20%, 1 until 75%, 1 -> 0 by 100% (smoothstep each ramp).
    Grip01 (pixel hands on the ledge): 0 -> 1 over 0..15%, 1 until 70%, 1 -> 0 by 90%, 0 after.
    CameraDip01: a smooth bump, 0 at 0, peak 1 at RiseShare (going over the edge), 0 at 1 (e.g. sin-based or two smoothsteps). */
struct FMantlePose { float ItemLower01, Grip01, CameraDip01; };
FMantlePose EvaluatePose(float Alpha, float RiseShare);
```

### Ledge detection (in `AGBPlayerCharacter`, e.g. `bool FindMantleLedge(FMantleLedge& Out) const`)
Using the capsule's world radius R and half height HH, Feet = location.Z - HH, Forward = yaw-only control forward:
1. **Wall:** sweep the player capsule (shrunk by 2 cm in radius) forward from the actor location by MantleProbeDistance
   on `ECC_Pawn` with the capsule's collision response params, ignoring self. Need a blocking hit, not start-penetrating,
   whose actor is not an `APawn` (never climb enemies), and whose `ImpactNormal` is near-horizontal (`|Normal.Z| < 0.3`).
   WallNormal2D = normalized XY of ImpactNormal. Require dot(Forward, -WallNormal2D) >= MantleFacingMinDot.
2. **Top:** sphere sweep (radius 8 cm) straight down at XY = ImpactPoint.XY - WallNormal2D * (MantleTopInset + 8),
   from Z = Feet + (max allowed height for this case) + 20 down to Z = Feet + (min height for this case) - 5. Need a
   blocking non-pawn hit, not start-penetrating, with `ImpactNormal.Z >= GetCharacterMovement()->GetWalkableFloorZ()`.
   LedgeTopZ = hit ImpactPoint.Z; LedgeHeight = LedgeTopZ - Feet. It must pass `CanMantleFromGround` / `CanMantleFromAir`.
3. **Room:** End = (ImpactPoint.XY - WallNormal2D * (R + MantleTopInset), LedgeTopZ + HH + 2). The capsule must fit at End
   and at Mid = (Start.XY, End.Z) (head room above the player): two `OverlapBlockingTestByChannel` with the capsule shape
   (same channel and response params), ignoring self. Either blocked -> no mantle.
4. Output: Start (actor location), End, the ledge edge point (ImpactPoint.XY, LedgeTopZ) for the HUD, the rise (End.Z - Start.Z).

### When it triggers
- **Jump pressed on the ground** (`IsMovingOnGround()`), in `InputJump` before `Jump()`: if a ledge is found with the
  ground limits (max = `JumpRise(JumpZVelocity, |GravityZ|*GravityScale)` + MantleMaxReach), start the mantle and do NOT jump.
  Otherwise the normal jump. (A ledge too high for one jump is a normal jump; the air rule below may still catch it,
  e.g. with the double jump.)
- **In the air** (`MOVE_Falling`, not dashing): every Tick, if a ledge is found with the air limits and the horizontal
  velocity is not moving away from the wall (dot(Velocity2D, -WallNormal2D) >= -50 cm/s), start the mantle. This is the
  "jumps and ends up at the edge" case, rising or falling.
- Never while: dead, control disabled, QTE active, dashing, movement frozen, already mantling.
- Make the jump press reachable by the smoke run: move the body of `InputJump` into a new public `void PressJump()` and
  have `InputJump` call it (same gates as today, plus "not mantling").

### During the mantle
- Start: `ReleaseHeldInputs()`, end any held primary/secondary as that already does; `StopMovementImmediately()`;
  movement mode `MOVE_Flying` keeping `JumpCurrentCount` (same trick as the dash). Store Start, End, ledge point, Duration, Elapsed.
- Tick: Elapsed += DeltaSeconds; `SetActorLocation(GBMantle::EvaluatePath(...))` (no sweep: the path was validated);
  velocity kept at zero. At Alpha >= 1: place at End, `SetMovementMode(MOVE_Walking)`, velocity zero, end.
- Blocked during the mantle: movement input (`ApplyMoveInput` / the QTE held-move path), jump, dash, primary, secondary,
  spell slots, reload, enchant, quick use, block, interact. Look (mouse) stays free.
- `CancelMantle()` (to Falling, everything visual back to rest) from: `HandleDeath`, `FreezeMovement`, `RespawnAt`,
  `LoadFromSnapshot`, `SetControlEnabled(false)`, `EndPlay`.
- Public read-only API for the HUD and the smoke run: `bool IsMantling() const`, `float GetMantleAlpha() const`,
  `FVector GetMantleLedgePoint() const`, `GBMantle::FMantlePose GetMantlePose() const` (zero pose when not mantling).

### The first-person animation
1. **Camera (view only, aim untouched):** pitch down by `CameraDip01 * 10` degrees and roll by `CameraDip01 * 3` degrees,
   plus a relative location drop of `ItemLower01 * 0` ... no: a drop of `Grip01 * 6` cm (the pull). Compose it with the
   existing view shake: `TickViewShake` must not overwrite it, and neither may leave a residue. Do it with one place that
   sets `Camera->SetRelativeRotation(Shake + Mantle)` and `Camera->SetRelativeLocation(Base eye + mantle offset)`, and
   returns exactly to zero / the base eye height when both are done (the base eye height comes from `BaseEyeHeight`).
   Keep these three numbers as named constants in the file's anonymous namespace ("feel and visual constants").
2. **Held item:** `HeldItemAnchor` relative location = `HeldItemOffset + FVector(-10, 0, -35) * ItemLower01` (the gun
   drops out of view), exactly `HeldItemOffset` at rest.
3. **Pixel hands (`AGBHUD::DrawHands`):** while mantling,
   - the normal pose (staff / gun hands / sword / bare hand / left hand / cast hand / shield) slides down off screen:
     add `ItemLower01 * Canvas->ClipY * 0.7` to the baseline `H` they are all placed from, so all of them go down together;
   - the two climbing hands: `hand_left` and `hand_right` sprites (existing) gripping the ledge. Project the ledge point
     to the screen (`Canvas->Project` or the player controller's `ProjectWorldLocationToScreen`); grip line Y = projected Y
     clamped to [0.12, 0.85] * ClipY (if the projection fails, 0.45 * ClipY). Hand centres at X = 0.38 W and 0.62 W. The
     knuckles (top of the sprite) sit on the grip line when Grip01 = 1; with Grip01 < 1 the hands are lowered by
     `(1 - Grip01) * (ClipY - GripY + sprite height)` (they come up from below the screen and go back down).
   - **Sleeves:** below each climbing hand, draw the sprite's cuff rows (the bottom 8 rows of the 20-row sprite: the
     purple `m` sleeve) repeated downward to the bottom of the screen, as a tile of the same texture with a UV sub-rect
     (nearest filtering, same pixel size P), so the arms reach up from the bottom edge. Look at how `DrawSprite` draws and
     add a small helper for the sub-rect tile.
   - Skip the cast hand and the raised shield while mantling.

### Test arena (`World/GBTestArena.cpp`): keep its gates honest with the new reach
The course and the platform were sized for jumps only; climbing adds `MantleMaxReach` (read it from Player.json like the
other stats there, default 160).
- The last course step (today `DoubleJumpStep = 1.5` jump rises) must need the double jump even with a climb:
  its rise = `1.5 * JumpRise + MantleMaxReach` (halfway between "one jump + climb" and "double jump + climb").
- `WallHeight`: 1100 -> 1400, and the warning check becomes `Top + 2 * JumpRise + MantleMaxReach > WallHeight - WallClearance`.
- New warning: if `2 * JumpRise + MantleMaxReach > PlatformTop - 20`, log that the past-era raised platform (future-only ramp) can be reached by climbing.
- Log the climb reach in the existing course `Display` line.

### Tests (pure logic only; file `Tests/GBPlayerTests.cpp`, flags like the existing ones)
- `Glyphbound.Player.MantleReach`: `CanMantleFromGround` true at MinHeight and at JumpRise + MaxReach, false just below
  MinHeight and just above JumpRise + MaxReach; `CanMantleFromAir` limits likewise; `JumpRise(800, 1568)` ~ 204.08.
- `Glyphbound.Player.MantlePath`: `EvaluatePath` exactly Start at 0 and End at 1; at RiseShare XY == Start.XY and Z == End.Z;
  Z never decreases over 50 samples; XY does not move before RiseShare; all `EvaluatePose` weights are 0 at 0 and at 1,
  `ItemLower01` is 1 at 0.5, `CameraDip01` peaks (max over samples) at RiseShare +- 0.05.
Each assertion must be able to fail for a wrong implementation (no constant copies). Do not name a test so that it is
also a folder of another test.

### Smoke steps (`Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`, names starting with `mantle:` so `gb.Smoke mantle` runs only them)
Add a block before the `quit` step (move later steps / quit as needed so nothing overlaps; look at how other blocks use
`MarkSim` and `MinSimSinceMark`). Use the arena's path-test wall (centre (-2500, -1150, 100), size (600, 100, 200):
its north face is at Y = -1100, top at Z = 200) and the raised platform (centre (2300, 2300), 1000 x 1000, top 600,
west face at X = 1800).
1. `mantle: ground press next to the 200 cm wall` - teleport the player on the floor at (-2500, -1100 + R + 5), yaw -90
   (facing the wall), velocity zero, then `PressJump()`. Log `SMOKE mantle ground started=%d` (IsMantling right after);
   fail (`UE_LOG(LogGB, Error, ...)`) if not started.
2. `mantle: screenshot mid-climb` - about 35% into the climb: `Shot(TEXT("mantle_grip"))` (the hands on the ledge).
3. `mantle: ground result` - 1 simulated second later: feet Z within 10 cm of 200 and Y < -1100 (on top of the wall),
   not mantling, camera relative rotation ~0 and `HeldItemAnchor` back at rest. Log and fail like above.
4. `mantle: wall too high is a normal jump` - teleport next to the platform's west face on the floor (X = 1800 - R - 5,
   Y = 2600, yaw 0), `PressJump()`: must NOT be mantling right after (600 cm is out of one jump + reach) and must be
   falling/jumping. Log and fail.
5. `mantle: air grab at the platform edge` - teleport into the air beside the platform's west face with the feet 120 cm
   below its top (centre Z = 600 - 120 + HH), yaw 0, `MOVE_Falling`, velocity zero. After 1 simulated second: feet within
   10 cm of 600 and X > 1800 (on the platform). Log and fail.
6. Put the player back where the next steps expect it (look at what the step after your block assumes), or at the
   arena start if nothing after depends on it.

## Rules
- **Iterate cheaply** (owner's rule, put in every brief): while working, compile only the Editor target
  (`powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1`), run only the anchored tests you touched
  (`powershell -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -Filter '^Glyphbound.Player.'`) and only your smoke steps without a window
  (`powershell -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Only mantle -Offscreen`). Do NOT run the full smoke, the game target or the
  full suite: the architect runs them once at the end. Long commands one at a time.
- Before any build or game run, check `Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock` ("who | what | UTC time"): if it exists and is
  younger than 45 minutes, another chat is building: wait and retry. While you build / run, write your own lock
  (`muse-mantle | build | <UTC>`) and delete it after.
- Never launch Play In Editor. Never open or close the Unreal Editor.
- Code comments and log text in English. Keep the existing style (tabs, `UE_LOG(LogGB, ...)`, `GB` prefixes).
- Do not commit; the architect reviews and commits.
- When done, report: files changed, build result, test result, the `SMOKE mantle` lines from the filtered smoke, and the
  path of the `mantle_grip` screenshot.

content.content:
## 9. Controls

| Action | Keyboard & mouse | Gamepad |
|---|---|---|
| Move | W A S D | Left stick |
| Look | Mouse | Right stick |
| Primary attack (staff: basic magic attack; gun: shoot) | Left click | R2 / RT |
| Aim (gun in hand) | Right click | L2 / LT |
| Spell slot 1 (staff in hand) | Right click | L1 / LB |
| Spell slots 2–5 (staff in hand) | 1, 2, 3, 4 | Hold L2 / LT + Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle (A, B, X, Y) |
| Reload (gun) | R | Standard shooter layout |
| Weapon enchant (gun in hand only) | T (R is reload) | L1 / LB (free with a gun in hand) |
| Switch staff ↔ gun (↔ sword) | Mouse wheel or Alt | D-pad up |
| Jump | Space | Cross (A) |
| Dash | Ctrl | Circle (B) |
| Quick-use item (grenade / potion / injection share one slot) | F | R1 / RB |
| Cycle the quick-use item | Shift | D-pad left / right |
| Interact (chests, portals, objects) | G | Triangle (Y) |
| Block: raise the summoned ice shield (staff or sword in hand; provisional keys) | Q (hold) | L2 / LT (hold) |
| QTE part 1 | W A S D | Face buttons |
| QTE part 2 | Mouse gesture | Right stick |
| Inventory | Tab | Options / View |
| Skill trees | K (also a tab inside the inventory) | From the inventory |
| Pause | Esc | Start / Menu |

Gun controls on gamepad follow the standard shooter layout.

Right click / L1 change meaning with the held weapon and never clash: staff = spell slot 1; gun = aim (right click) and enchant (L1). L2 means "spell modifier" with the staff and "aim" with a gun.

No sprint (the air speed passive covers movement speed).

Menus (inventory, skill trees, pause) work with keyboard, gamepad **and mouse**: the cursor is visible while a menu is open and a click does what confirm does.

## 18. Provisional rules and numbers picked by the architect (2026-11-12)
The owner asked the architect not to stop for missing design details. Everything below was chosen so the prototype could be built; **all of it is provisional** and waits for the owner's word. Numbers are in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and can be changed there without touching code.

### Rules
- **Jumps commit to their direction (owner, 2026-11-12):** like a real jump, the direction cannot be changed in the air (air control 0; the same when walking off a ledge). The direction is chosen at takeoff: the movement keys held at that moment. The second jump can choose a new direction and then commits again. Provisional details (architect): a jump from standing with a direction held leaves at 60% of walking speed at least; the second jump with a direction held leaves at walking speed at least, and with no direction held it keeps the current drift. The dash still works in the air and is not affected.
- **Double jump on day 1:** the player starts knowing the air passive "Double jump" so it can be tested now. In the real game it is learned in the air zone (§6); remove it from `Player.json` `StartingSpells` then.
- **Dash:** available from the start (the air passive only improves it). It goes in the movement direction (forward when standing still), works in the air, gives no invulnerability, and does not refill jumps.
### Numbers (first pass, all in the JSON files)

# Code review: ledge climb (mantle) in Glyphbound (UE 5.9 C++)

Review the uncommitted changes in this repository (`git diff` and new untracked files under
`Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound`, plus `Glyphbound/Content/Data/Player.json`). Read-only: do not edit anything.

The spec the implementer followed is `Prompts/mantle_climb.md`; the design rule is in `Design/GDD.md` §18 "Ledge climb".
The game is first person: the climb is a camera dip, the held item lowered, and 2D pixel hands drawn by `AGBHUD::DrawHands`.

Look for concrete defects, with a failure scenario for each:
- Ledge detection: wrong traces/channels, climbing pawns, climbing from behind/sideways, false positives on slopes or
  steps, start-penetrating hits, the capsule ending inside geometry or a ceiling, wrong heights (feet vs centre).
- Trigger rules: jump press on the ground climbs only when one jump + reach covers the top; the air grab, rising or
  falling, not when moving away; never while dead, dashing, in the QTE, frozen or already climbing.
- State: movement mode restore (Flying -> Walking), jump count, cancel paths (death, respawn, load, freeze, control
  off, EndPlay), inputs left blocked or held after the climb, time dilation.
- View: camera relative rotation/location and `HeldItemAnchor` must return exactly to rest and must compose with the
  existing view shake without residue; aim (control rotation) must not change.
- HUD: projection fallback, divide-by-zero, sprite UV sub-rect math, drawing when the sprite is missing.
- Pure functions in `Player/GBMantle.*` and the two tests `Glyphbound.Player.MantleReach` / `MantlePath`: could a wrong
  implementation pass them?
- Smoke steps `mantle:` in `Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`: do they really check what they claim, and do they leave the player
  where later steps expect?
- Test arena changes in `World/GBTestArena.cpp`.

Report findings ranked by severity as: [P1/P2/P3] title — file:line — failure scenario — fix. If there are none, say so.

El escalado está en marcha; todavía no hay nada compilado, revisado ni subido.

**Cómo funcionará:**
- **En el aire:** si saltas y quedas frente al borde de una estructura que estás mirando, y su parte de arriba está a 1,6 m o menos por encima de tus pies, el personaje se agarra y sube solo. Funciona tanto subiendo como cayendo.
- **Pegado a un bloque y pulsando salto:** si con un salto se alcanza el borde (unos 2 m de salto más los 1,6 m de alcance de las manos), escala en vez de saltar. Si el bloque es más alto, salta normal, y con el doble salto todavía puede agarrarse en el aire. Tiene que haber sitio arriba y encima de la cabeza, y nunca se escala a un enemigo.
- **La animación:** el juego es en primera persona y no hay cuerpo con esqueleto, así que la animación es de cámara:
  - el arma o el bastón baja y sale de la vista;
  - las dos manos pixel-art suben desde abajo con sus mangas y se agarran al borde, en el punto donde se ve en pantalla;
  - la cámara se inclina un poco al pasar por encima;
  - después las manos se sueltan y el arma vuelve.
- Escalar dura unos 0,2 s más 0,18 s por metro de subida. Mientras dura no se puede disparar, lanzar hechizos ni hacer dash; mirar con el ratón sí.

**Un efecto que tuve que corregir en el mapa de pruebas:** escalar permite llegar más alto.
- El último escalón del circuito sigue exigiendo el doble salto.
- Los muros exteriores pasan de 11 a 14 m para que no se puedan saltar.
- Si alguien cambia los números, el mapa avisará si la plataforma de 6 m de la era pasada se puede alcanzar escalando.

Todos los números son provisionales y se pueden cambiar en `Player.json`. La regla ya está en el GDD (v0.44).

Ahora mismo Muse lo está programando a partir del encargo en `Prompts/mantle_climb.md`, con pruebas automáticas que suben un muro de 2 m y se agarran al borde de la plataforma. Cuando termine: compilo, paso las pruebas y la revisión de Sol 6.1, corro el smoke completo y hago commit y push. Al final necesitaré que una persona lo pruebe jugando, porque los agentes no lanzan PIE.
