# Block: the weapon skill tree becomes a hub of gun branches, Cyberpunk style; skill pages take their tree's look (Nov 13, CENTRAL)

> Written by the architect chat of this block (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). To be merged into the day entry by whoever closes the day. Times in UTC.

## The owner's notes
After the package `194e9ab`, the owner sent two screenshots (`media/2026-11-13/weaponhub_owner_report_weapons.webp`, `weaponhub_owner_report_spells.webp`) and wrote, in Spanish:

> *"al estar en skill - weapons deberia cambiarse toda la interfaz. Para el de spells hayy que cambiar el fondo para uno que haga mejor contraste con el contenido. Y vamos a hacerle una pequeña reforma del skill tree de armas. Vamos a hacerlo un poco estilo cyberpunk con las ramas. El primer perk sigue siendo el mismo, que es Heavy Rounds. Y de ese van a salir las 3 ramas. Sin embargo, esto va a ser con submenús, similar a Cyberpunk. De Heavy Rounds van a salir las 3 categorías, que son escopeta, rifle y pistola. Y al hacer clic en esas esferas, cuadros o símbolos, se abre el skill tree respectivo de esa arma. En la interfaz tiene que haber también un botón para que el jugador pueda volver, ya que esta es dentro de un submenú."*

Translation: "On Skills > Weapons the whole interface should change. For the spells one, the background must change to one that contrasts better with the content. And let's give the weapon skill tree a small reform, a bit Cyberpunk style with the branches. The first perk is still Heavy Rounds, and the 3 branches come out of it. But this will be with submenus, like Cyberpunk. Out of Heavy Rounds come the 3 categories: shotgun, rifle and pistol. Clicking those spheres, boxes or symbols opens that weapon's skill tree. The interface must also have a button for the player to go back, since this is inside a submenu."

## What changed
- **The whole screen follows the shown tree (`UI/GBHUD.cpp`, `GetMenuSkin`).** On the Skill Trees screen and on the inventory's Skills page, the weapons page is cyberpunk from title to footer and the spells page is RPG, whatever the era. The other shared menus keep following the era, as decided in the previous block.
- **The spell page's background.** It used to be bricks behind bricks, and the gold-framed nodes fought the pattern. Now the panel is near-black slate with a faint trace of the masonry and a low ember warmth in the middle (`weaponhub_spells_dark_background_1080.png`).
- **The weapon hub (`UI/GBHUD_Menus.cpp`).**
  - Heavy Rounds sits on top. Under it hang three emblems, numbered 01 to 03: **Pistol, Rifle, Shotgun**. Each has a pixel outline of its gun, its name and one segment per rank of its perks.
  - Enter or a click on an emblem opens that gun's page. The page has a **Back** button with the Esc key next to it, and the title "WEAPONS // RIFLE". Esc and gamepad B also go back to the hub, landing on that gun's emblem.
  - The emblems are not perks: `GetSkillNodes` builds them as pseudo-nodes (`Branch_<Gun>`) that never reach the skill component.
  - The page shown is always derived from the cursor. So the mouse, the keyboard, the tabs and the memory of the last node in each tree all work unchanged.
  - The weapon pages are centred vertically. The first try left the bottom half of the hub empty (`weaponhub_hub_first_try_1080.png`).
- **Data (`Skills.json`, new `Branch` field in `FGBSkillNodeDefinition`).** The owner named the categories but not their contents. The architect regrouped the nine existing perks by theme, **with their effects, costs and ranks unchanged**, so §19's balance and the 36-point budget still hold:
  - **Pistol** (precision): Deadeye; Marksman -> Precision Recovery.
  - **Rifle** (sustained fire): Long Shot; Quick Trigger -> Steady Grip.
  - **Shotgun** (close range): Point Blank -> Arcane Conduit; Rapid Reload.
  - Two prerequisites changed so each branch stands alone: Rapid Reload now needs Heavy Rounds (it needed Quick Trigger), and Arcane Conduit needs Point Blank (it needed Marksman).
  - The three perks that work on every gun now say "All guns:" in their description.
  - GDD v0.39 records this as provisional. Gun-specific versions of the shared perks are the obvious next step if the owner wants each branch to touch only its gun.
- **Smoke:** the Arcane Conduit step unlocks Point Blank instead of Marksman, because of the new prerequisite. The `12_weapon_tree` screenshot shows the hub. The UI block now captures the hub (`ui_21`, `ui_20`) and a gun page (`ui_09`, Rifle).

## Review: GPT Sol 6.1 (Codex CLI, medium, read-only, logged through `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`)
Prompt: `Prompts/weapon_hub_review_sol.md`. **One finding, real, fixed.**
- **The problem:** inside menus, Tab was mapped to "back". On a gun page in the inventory, Tab would go back to the hub instead of closing the inventory, which is Tab's own job.
- **The fix:** Tab now has its own menu action (`MenuTabKey`). In the inventory it closes the inventory, like I. On every other screen it still acts as "back", as before.

Sol also confirmed:
- No pseudo-node reaches the progression code.
- Opening and going back both clear the stale mouse hits.
- The look always matches the page that is drawn.
- All 22 perks are still reachable.
- The balance tool still runs, and its builds satisfy the new prerequisites.

# Block: the player climbs ledges (Nov 13, CENTRAL)

> Written by the architect chat of this block (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). To be merged into the day entry by whoever closes the day. Times in UTC.

## The owner's request
Original prompt (Spanish):

> *"Quiero que cuando el personaje salta y queda en el borde de una estructura, haga la animacion de escalar y suba dicha estructura. Tambien cuando el personaje esta pegado a un bloque/estructura y presiona el salto, si el salto es lo suficientemente alto, que haga la animacion de escalar dicha estructura/bloque en vez de saltar."*

Translation: "When the character jumps and ends up at the edge of a structure, it should play the climb animation and climb that structure. Also, when the character is right against a block/structure and presses jump, if the jump is high enough, it should play the climb animation and climb that structure/block instead of jumping."

## Design decisions (architect, provisional; GDD v0.44, §18 "Ledge climb")
- **First person, so the "climb animation" is first-person.** The player has no body mesh: the hands are 2D pixel-art sprites drawn by the HUD and guns are 3D models under the camera. The climb is the camera dipping 10° (with 3° of roll) as it goes over the edge, the held item dropping out of view, and both pixel hands coming up from the bottom of the screen with their sleeves and gripping the ledge where it projects on screen. No new art: the existing `hand_left` / `hand_right` sprites, with the cuff rows tiled downward as sleeves.
- **Two triggers.**
  - In the air, rising or falling: the climb starts on its own when the view faces a wall (within 60°), and the wall's top is 15 cm to 1.6 m above the feet.
  - Jump pressed on the ground: the climb happens instead of the jump when the top is between 0.5 m and one jump's rise (2.04 m) plus 1.6 m. A higher wall is a normal jump, and the double jump can still end in an air climb.
- **"Facing the wall" is required.** Jumps commit to their direction (air control 0), so the view is the clearest sign of intent. Without it, strafing along a wall would grab it.
- **The test arena's gates had to be re-sized.** The climb adds up to 1.6 m of reach on top of every jump. Measured with the arena's own formulas:
  - The course's last step (1.5 jump rises = 3.06 m) became reachable with one jump plus a climb (3.64 m). It now rises 1.5 jump rises **plus** the reach (4.66 m): halfway between "one jump + climb" and "double jump + climb".
  - From the course top, a double jump plus a climb reached 12.8 m, over the 11 m outer walls. The walls are now 14 m.
  - The past-era raised platform (6 m, future-only ramp) stays out of reach: a double jump plus a climb gives 5.68 m. A new warning fires if the numbers ever change that.
- All the numbers are stats in `Player.json` (`Mantle*`), read with modifiers like the other movement stats. Only the view feel (dip, roll, pull, item drop) is code constants.

## How it was built
1. **Brief** `Prompts/mantle_climb.md` (architect): the full design, ledge detection, trigger rules, the view and HUD animation, the arena changes, two pure-logic tests and a `mantle:` smoke block.
2. **Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor (High) via OpenCode** (run `191856-opencode-faf360`, default implementer) implemented it in about 25 minutes. New pure module `Player/GBMantle.*`, the player state machine, `AGBHUD::DrawMantleHands`, the arena, the tests and 8 smoke steps.
   - It found a real bug on its own: the forward wall sweep started flush with the floor and hit it, so the jump-press climb never started. It lifted the sweep 5 cm.
   - It reported that its screenshots were unreliable in filtered runs.
3. **The architect checked the screenshots itself** (rule: self-review art before delivering). The two climb shots showed no hands at all. A state log at the moment of each shot said the climb was running with the hands at full grip, so the problem was in the drawing. There were two causes:
   - **The hands were hidden behind the RPG status bar.** At 68% of the climb the ledge is already below the view, the clamp put the hands at the screen bottom, and the bar is drawn over them. Also, the shot was taken too late.
   - **The camera never dipped.** The camera follows the pawn's control rotation (`bUsePawnControlRotation`), and the engine overwrites its rotation every view (`UCameraComponent::GetCameraView`, checked in the 5.9 source), so any relative rotation is thrown away. **This also means the existing view shake (spell interrupts, GDD 18) has never been visible since it was added.** The view offsets now go through the camera's additive offset, which the engine applies after the control rotation. The shake works too.
4. **Review: GPT Sol 6.1** (Codex CLI, medium, read-only, run `194720-codex-635804`, prompt `Prompts/mantle_climb_review_sol.md`). Six findings, all accepted and fixed:
   - P1: the climb only checked the capsule at the corner and at the end, so a thin ceiling in between could be passed through. Both path segments are now capsule sweeps.
   - P2: the camera dip was overwritten. Same finding as the architect's, found independently.
   - P2: a thin beam can pass the top check with nothing under the capsule's centre. The climb now needs walkable floor under the end point.
   - P2: releasing jump during a climb (the movement mode is Flying) resets the jump count, so a cancelled climb refilled the double jump. The count is saved and restored on cancel.
   - P3: the tests would pass a "hands never show" or a "teleport across" implementation, and the limits only used default numbers. Asserts were added for mid-path progress, another rise share, interior grip values, non-default reach numbers and another jump.
   - P3: the smoke accepted any non-ground mode as a "normal jump", and a climb still in progress as finished. It now needs Falling plus 10 cm of rise, and walking on top after the climb.
5. **HUD placement, judged on screenshots.** The hands first sat over the status bar's centre crest (only the knuckles showed). They moved out to 27% / 73% of the width, and their lowest grip line keeps the whole hand and some sleeve above the bar. Final shots: `media/2026-11-13/ledgeclimb_grip_ground_720.png` (climbing the 2 m wall from a jump press) and `ledgeclimb_grip_air_720.png` (air grab at the platform edge).
6. **Smoke screenshots in filtered runs.** A filtered run starts its first step 1 s after the map loads, while frames still hitch, and a screenshot can capture an older frame. The `mantle:` block now waits 3 s first, and each climb shot freezes time (world time dilation 0.01) until the next step, so the shot shows the climb at a known moment.

## Exception to the default implementer
The fixes after the review were made by the architect chat itself, not sent back to Muse. They were six small, precise changes that the architect had already diagnosed from engine source and screenshots, plus HUD placement judged image by image. Writing a brief would have cost more than making them.

## Checks
- Iteration: Editor target only, `^Glyphbound.Player.` tests (3 green), `Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Only mantle -Offscreen` (about 22 s per run). Climb results: wall top feet 202 cm (expected 200 ± 10), platform 602 cm (600 ± 10), the 6 m wall is a normal jump (138 cm of rise, not climbing), view and held item exactly at rest after the climb.
- End of block: game target build, full test suite and full smoke (results in the commit message).

## Tools
Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, architect), OpenCode with Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor (High), Codex CLI with GPT Sol 6.1 (review), Unreal Engine 5.9.0.

## Open for the owner
The reach (1.6 m), the speed (0.22 s + 0.18 s per metre) and the "must face the wall" rule are provisional. Playing it is the real test: agents do not run PIE.

content.text:
El escalado funciona en las pruebas filtradas. Ahora corre la verificación completa (build del juego, todos los tests y el smoke entero); el commit con push va al terminar.

**Resultado de las pruebas filtradas:**
- **Salto pegado a un muro de 2 m:** escala en vez de saltar y queda arriba (pies a 202 cm).
- **Agarre en el aire en el borde de la plataforma de 6 m:** sube solo y termina caminando arriba (602 cm).
- **Muro demasiado alto (6 m desde el suelo):** hace un salto normal, sin escalar.
- Al acabar, la cámara y el arma quedan exactamente en reposo.

**Problemas que encontré al mirar yo las capturas** (las de Muse no servían):
- **No se veían las manos:** quedaban detrás de la barra de estado. Ahora salen a los lados con las mangas, empujando hacia abajo sobre el borde. Las capturas están en `Devlog/media/2026-11-13/ledgeclimb_grip_*.png`.
- **La cámara no se inclinaba:** el motor sobrescribe la rotación de la cámara en cada fotograma. Al arreglarlo apareció un fallo más antiguo: **la sacudida de cámara al interrumpir un hechizo nunca se ha visto desde que se añadió**. Con el mismo arreglo ahora sí funciona.

**Revisión de Sol 6.1:** encontró seis fallos y los arreglé todos. Los más importantes:
- el escalado podía atravesar un techo fino;
- podía terminar sobre un saliente sin suelo debajo;
- si se cancelaba a medias, devolvía el doble salto ya gastado.

Los arreglos los hice yo en vez de devolvérselos a Muse; lo dejé anotado en `Devlog/days/2026-11-13_ledge_climb_block.md`.

**Para decidir al probarlo** (todo provisional y ajustable en `Player.json`):
- el alcance: hasta 1,6 m por encima de los pies;
- la velocidad: 0,22 s más 0,18 s por metro;
- que haya que estar mirando al muro.

Hace falta que alguien lo pruebe jugando, porque los agentes no lanzan PIE.

content.text:
El escalado ya está hecho, con commit y push (`9bf924a`), pero nadie lo ha probado jugando todavía.

**Verificación final:**
- Compilan el Editor y el juego.
- Los 47 tests están en verde.
- El smoke completo sale limpio.
- Pruebas del escalado:
  - **Salto pegado al muro de 2 m:** sube y queda encima.
  - **Agarre en el aire en la plataforma de 6 m:** termina caminando arriba.
  - **Muro de 6 m desde el suelo:** salta normal.
  - Al terminar, la cámara y el arma quedan exactamente en reposo.

**Cómo se ve:** el arma baja y desaparece, y las dos manos pixel-art suben con sus mangas y se agarran al borde. Luego la cámara se inclina al pasar por encima y el arma vuelve. Las capturas están en `Devlog/media/2026-11-13/ledgeclimb_grip_*.png`.

**Además:** la sacudida de cámara al interrumpir un hechizo no se veía nunca, porque el motor sobrescribía la rotación. Con el mismo arreglo del escalado ahora sí se ve.

**Al probarlo, conviene ajustar** (todo provisional en `Player.json`):
- el alcance de las manos: 1,6 m por encima de los pies;
- la velocidad: 0,22 s más 0,18 s por metro;
- la regla de que hay que estar mirando al muro.

**Registro:** la regla está en el GDD (v0.44) y el proceso en `Devlog/days/2026-11-13_ledge_climb_block.md`, con el prompt original, la traducción y la nota de que los arreglos de la revisión los hice yo.

GitHub avisó de que la transcripción de otra sesión de hoy pesa 55 MB. Pasa del tamaño recomendado (50 MB), pero no del límite, que es de 100 MB; aun así conviene vigilarlo si sigue creciendo.

# Task: climb ledges in any direction, not only the one the view faces — Glyphbound (UE 5.9, C++)

You are the implementer. Read `C:\GameJam\CLAUDE.md` (rules). Do NOT edit `Design/GDD.md` or the dev log. Do not commit.

## Owner's request (translated from Spanish)
"Make it possible to climb without looking at the wall, for example with your back to it."

## Current state (commit 9bf924a, read it first)
- `Player/GBMantle.h/.cpp`: pure climb math (tested by `Glyphbound.Player.MantleReach` / `MantlePath` in `Tests/GBPlayerTests.cpp`).
- `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.cpp`: `FindMantleLedge(Out, bFromGround)` sweeps the capsule along the view's yaw forward and
  requires `dot(Forward2D, -WallNormal2D) >= MantleFacingMinDot`; `PressJump()` climbs on the ground; `Tick` grabs in the air
  (`Approach >= -50` check); `StartMantle`, `TickMantle`, `CancelMantle`, `ApplyCameraPose` (view offsets via the camera's
  additive offset), `LastMoveInput` = the held movement input (x = right, y = forward), `GetMoveInputWorldDirection`.
- `UI/GBHUD.cpp` `DrawMantleHands`: the hands grip where the ledge projects on screen.
- Smoke block `mantle:` in `Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`.

## Design (architect, provisional)
### Which directions are searched (probe directions)
The wall is no longer looked for along the view. `FindMantleLedge` takes a probe direction (2D unit vector) and checks
`dot(ProbeDir, -WallNormal2D) >= MantleApproachMinDot` (the sweep must meet the wall roughly head-on) instead of the view.
A new pure function picks the ordered list of directions to try:
```
/** Directions to probe for a ledge, in priority order (2D unit vectors).
    - Intent given (non-zero IntentDir): only that direction (the player chose where to go).
    - No intent: 8 directions 45 degrees apart, starting with ViewForward, then +-45, +-90, +-135, 180
      (positive = counterclockwise first), so the nearest to the view wins. */
void GetProbeDirections(const FVector2D& ViewForward, const FVector2D& IntentDir, TArray<FVector2D>& Out);
```
The first direction that finds a valid ledge wins.
- **Jump pressed on the ground:** intent = the held movement input's world direction (`GetMoveInputWorldDirection(LastMoveInput)`).
  So: standing still with the back to a wall + jump = climb it; holding S (backwards) into a wall + jump = climb it; holding
  W away from a wall behind + jump = a normal forward jump (never a climb behind the player).
- **In the air:** intent = the horizontal velocity direction when its speed is at least `MantleAirSearchMinSpeed`
  (jumps commit to their direction, so the velocity is the intent); slower (a vertical jump, or after hitting a wall, which
  stops the velocity into it) = no intent, all 8 directions. The existing "not moving away" check (`Approach >= -50`) stays,
  against the found wall.
- Cost: the 8-direction search runs only when there is no intent; keep the cheap checks first (the wall sweep) and stop at the
  first hit. No per-tick allocations (use a `TArray` with inline allocator or a fixed array).

### The view turns to the wall
When the climb starts, if the wall faces away from the view by more than `MantleTurnMinAngle` degrees (angle between the
view's yaw forward and -WallNormal2D), the view's yaw turns to face the wall during the climb, so the player ends up on
top looking across it and the hands grip a ledge that is on screen:
- Total turn = the signed shortest yaw delta from the view yaw to the wall-facing yaw (-WallNormal2D), computed at start.
  (No turn when the angle is at most `MantleTurnMinAngle`.)
- Pure: `float TurnFraction(float Alpha, float RiseShare)` = smoothstep from 0 at Alpha 0 to 1 at Alpha = RiseShare, 1 after.
- Each mantle tick, add `(TurnFraction(Alpha) - TurnFraction(PrevAlpha)) * TotalTurn` to the control rotation's yaw
  (deltas, so the mouse still works during the climb and both add up). Only yaw; pitch untouched. Cancel stops turning.
- `CanMantleNow`, inputs, cancel paths, camera dip, held item and HUD hands stay as they are.

### Data (`Content/Data/Player.json` "Stats", constants in `Core/GBStatNames.h`)
- Rename `MantleFacingMinDot` -> `MantleApproachMinDot` (value 0.5; comment: the probe direction must meet the wall at most
  60 degrees off its normal). Remove the old name everywhere.
- New `MantleAirSearchMinSpeed` = 150 (cm/s: in the air, slower than this searches all around).
- New `MantleTurnMinAngle` = 60 (degrees: a wall further off the view than this turns the view to it during the climb).

### Tests (pure, `Tests/GBPlayerTests.cpp`; new test `Glyphbound.Player.MantleProbe`)
- With intent: exactly one direction, equal to the normalized intent (also when the intent is not normalized).
- Without intent: 8 directions, all unit length, the first equals ViewForward, the last is -ViewForward, all 8 distinct and
  45 degrees apart as a set (each one's nearest neighbour is 45 degrees away), the second and third are +45 and -45.
- A different ViewForward rotates the whole list (not fixed world axes).
- `TurnFraction`: 0 at 0, 1 at RiseShare and at 1, strictly between at RiseShare / 2, non-decreasing over 50 samples, and
  for two different RiseShares the value at 0.3 differs.
Each assertion must be able to fail for a wrong implementation.

### Smoke (`Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`, names starting with `mantle:`; add before the "back to the arena start" step,
shift later steps and `quit` so nothing overlaps)
1. `mantle: back to the 200 cm wall, standing jump press` - same spot as the existing ground step
   (X -2500, Y = -1100 + R + 5, on the floor) but yaw +90 (back to the wall), velocity zero, `LastMoveInput` empty
   (it is protected: call `ReleaseHeldInputs()` or add nothing; check it is zero), then `PressJump()`. Log
   `SMOKE mantle back started=%d`; fail if not started.
2. `mantle: back climb result` - after 1 simulated second: feet within 10 cm of 200, Y < -1100, not mantling, walking,
   and the control yaw within 15 degrees of -90 (the view turned to the wall). Log and fail.
3. `mantle: back to the platform, air grab` - in the air beside the platform's west face (X = 1800 - R - 5, Y 2600,
   feet 120 cm under the top 600), yaw 180 (back to the platform), MOVE_Falling, velocity zero. After 1 simulated second:
   feet within 10 cm of 600, X > 1800, walking, control yaw within 15 degrees of 0. Log and fail.
4. `mantle: holding away from a wall behind is a jump` - needs a held move input: add a small public test hook on the
   player, `void SetMoveInputForTest(const FVector2D& Input)` (sets `LastMoveInput` and `LastMoveInputFrame = GFrameCounter`),
   used only by the smoke. Spot of step 1, yaw +90 (back to the wall), input (0, 1) = forward (away from the wall),
   `PressJump()`: must NOT be mantling. Log and fail.
Keep the existing `mantle:` steps working (they face the wall; with no input they still find it first).

## Rules
- **Iterate cheaply** (owner's rule): compile only the Editor target (`powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1`), run only
  `powershell -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -Filter '^Glyphbound.Player.'` and
  `powershell -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Only mantle -Offscreen`. Do NOT run the full smoke, the game target or the
  full suite: the architect runs them once at the end. One long command at a time.
- Before any build or game run check `Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock`: younger than 45 minutes = another chat is building,
  wait. While you build/run write `muse-mantle | build | <UTC>` there and delete it after.
- Never launch Play In Editor, never open or close the Unreal Editor.
- English comments and logs, existing style. Do not commit.
- Report: files changed, build, tests, the `SMOKE mantle` lines.

## Owner's request (translated from Spanish)
"Make it possible to climb without looking at the wall, for example with your back to it."

## Current state (commit 9bf924a, read it first)
- `Player/GBMantle.h/.cpp`: pure climb math (tested by `Glyphbound.Player.MantleReach` / `MantlePath` in `Tests/GBPlayerTests.cpp`).
- `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.cpp`: `FindMantleLedge(Out, bFromGround)` sweeps the capsule along the view's yaw forward and
  requires `dot(Forward2D, -WallNormal2D) >= MantleFacingMinDot`; `PressJump()` climbs on the ground; `Tick` grabs in the air
  (`Approach >= -50` check); `StartMantle`, `TickMantle`, `CancelMantle`, `ApplyCameraPose` (view offsets via the camera's
  additive offset), `LastMoveInput` = the held movement input (x = right, y = forward), `GetMoveInputWorldDirection`.
- `UI/GBHUD.cpp` `DrawMantleHands`: the hands grip where the ledge projects on screen.
- Smoke block `mantle:` in `Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`.

## Design (architect, provisional)
### Which directions are searched (probe directions)
The wall is no longer looked for along the view. `FindMantleLedge` takes a probe direction (2D unit vector) and checks
`dot(ProbeDir, -WallNormal2D) >= MantleApproachMinDot` (the sweep must meet the wall roughly head-on) instead of the view.
A new pure function picks the ordered list of directions to try:
```
/** Directions to probe for a ledge, in priority order (2D unit vectors).
    - Intent given (non-zero IntentDir): only that direction (the player chose where to go).
    - No intent: 8 directions 45 degrees apart, starting with ViewForward, then +-45, +-90, +-135, 180
      (positive = counterclockwise first), so the nearest to the view wins. */
void GetProbeDirections(const FVector2D& ViewForward, const FVector2D& IntentDir, TArray<FVector2D>& Out);
```
The first direction that finds a valid ledge wins.
- **Jump pressed on the ground:** intent = the held movement input's world direction (`GetMoveInputWorldDirection(LastMoveInput)`).
  So: standing still with the back to a wall + jump = climb it; holding S (backwards) into a wall + jump = climb it; holding
  W away from a wall behind + jump = a normal forward jump (never a climb behind the player).
- **In the air:** intent = the horizontal velocity direction when its speed is at least `MantleAirSearchMinSpeed`
  (jumps commit to their direction, so the velocity is the intent); slower (a vertical jump, or after hitting a wall, which
  stops the velocity into it) = no intent, all 8 directions. The existing "not moving away" check (`Approach >= -50`) stays,
  against the found wall.
- Cost: the 8-direction search runs only when there is no intent; keep the cheap checks first (the wall sweep) and stop at the
  first hit. No per-tick allocations (use a `TArray` with inline allocator or a fixed array).

### The view turns to the wall
When the climb starts, if the wall faces away from the view by more than `MantleTurnMinAngle` degrees (angle between the
view's yaw forward and -WallNormal2D), the view's yaw turns to face the wall during the climb, so the player ends up on
top looking across it and the hands grip a ledge that is on screen:
- Total turn = the signed shortest yaw delta from the view yaw to the wall-facing yaw (-WallNormal2D), computed at start.
  (No turn when the angle is at most `MantleTurnMinAngle`.)
- Pure: `float TurnFraction(float Alpha, float RiseShare)` = smoothstep from 0 at Alpha 0 to 1 at Alpha = RiseShare, 1 after.
- Each mantle tick, add `(TurnFraction(Alpha) - TurnFraction(PrevAlpha)) * TotalTurn` to the control rotation's yaw
  (deltas, so the mouse still works during the climb and both add up). Only yaw; pitch untouched. Cancel stops turning.
- `CanMantleNow`, inputs, cancel paths, camera dip, held item and HUD hands stay as they are.

### Data (`Content/Data/Player.json` "Stats", constants in `Core/GBStatNames.h`)
- Rename `MantleFacingMinDot` -> `MantleApproachMinDot` (value 0.5; comment: the probe direction must meet the wall at most
  60 degrees off its normal). Remove the old name everywhere.
- New `MantleAirSearchMinSpeed` = 150 (cm/s: in the air, slower than this searches all around).
- New `MantleTurnMinAngle` = 60 (degrees: a wall further off the view than this turns the view to it during the climb).

### Tests (pure, `Tests/GBPlayerTests.cpp`; new test `Glyphbound.Player.MantleProbe`)
- With intent: exactly one direction, equal to the normalized intent (also when the intent is not normalized).
- Without intent: 8 directions, all unit length, the first equals ViewForward, the last is -ViewForward, all 8 distinct and
  45 degrees apart as a set (each one's nearest neighbour is 45 degrees away), the second and third are +45 and -45.
- A different ViewForward rotates the whole list (not fixed world axes).
- `TurnFraction`: 0 at 0, 1 at RiseShare and at 1, strictly between at RiseShare / 2, non-decreasing over 50 samples, and
  for two different RiseShares the value at 0.3 differs.
Each assertion must be able to fail for a wrong implementation.

### Smoke (`Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`, names starting with `mantle:`; add before the "back to the arena start" step,
shift later steps and `quit` so nothing overlaps)
1. `mantle: back to the 200 cm wall, standing jump press` - same spot as the existing ground step
   (X -2500, Y = -1100 + R + 5, on the floor) but yaw +90 (back to the wall), velocity zero, `LastMoveInput` empty
   (it is protected: call `ReleaseHeldInputs()` or add nothing; check it is zero), then `PressJump()`. Log
   `SMOKE mantle back started=%d`; fail if not started.
2. `mantle: back climb result` - after 1 simulated second: feet within 10 cm of 200, Y < -1100, not mantling, walking,
   and the control yaw within 15 degrees of -90 (the view turned to the wall). Log and fail.
3. `mantle: back to the platform, air grab` - in the air beside the platform's west face (X = 1800 - R - 5, Y 2600,
   feet 120 cm under the top 600), yaw 180 (back to the platform), MOVE_Falling, velocity zero. After 1 simulated second:
   feet within 10 cm of 600, X > 1800, walking, control yaw within 15 degrees of 0. Log and fail.
4. `mantle: holding away from a wall behind is a jump` - needs a held move input: add a small public test hook on the
   player, `void SetMoveInputForTest(const FVector2D& Input)` (sets `LastMoveInput` and `LastMoveInputFrame = GFrameCounter`),
   used only by the smoke. Spot of step 1, yaw +90 (back to the wall), input (0, 1) = forward (away from the wall),
   `PressJump()`: must NOT be mantling. Log and fail.
Keep the existing `mantle:` steps working (they face the wall; with no input they still find it first).

## Rules
- **Iterate cheaply** (owner's rule): compile only the Editor target (`powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1`), run only
  `powershell -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -Filter '^Glyphbound.Player.'` and
  `powershell -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1 -Only mantle -Offscreen`. Do NOT run the full smoke, the game target or the
  full suite: the architect runs them once at the end. One long command at a time.
- Before any build or game run check `Glyphbound/Saved/machine.lock`: younger than 45 minutes = another chat is building,
  wait. While you build/run write `muse-mantle | build | <UTC>` there and delete it after.
- Never launch Play In Editor, never open or close the Unreal Editor.
- English comments and logs, existing style. Do not commit.
- Report: files changed, build, tests, the `SMOKE mantle` lines.

lines: > Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
-> Status: **v0.44, 2026-11-13** — owner's vision plus fourteen rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
+> Status: **v0.45, 2026-11-13** — owner's vision plus fifteen rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.

> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Implementation is delegated as `CLAUDE.md` says ("Implementador").
> Project code name: **Glyphbound** (provisional; the game title is still TBD). Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.

+- v0.45 (2026-11-13): owner: **climbing does not need the view on the wall** ("with your back to it, for example"). The climb now follows the player's intent: the held direction on the ground, the jump's direction in the air, and all around when there is none. When the wall is behind or beside the view, the view turns to it during the climb (architect, provisional; §18 "Ledge climb").

- v0.44 (2026-11-13): owner: **the player climbs ledges**. A jump that ends at the edge of a structure climbs onto it, and pressing jump right against a block climbs it instead of jumping when one jump can reach its top. In first person the climb is the camera dipping over the edge, the held item dropping out of view and the two pixel hands gripping the ledge. Architect, provisional: the reach, durations and the "facing the wall" rule (§18 "Ledge climb"); the test arena's gates were re-sized for the extra reach.

- v0.43 (2026-11-13): owner: **the weapon enchant's element is chosen in its QTE**, always in the same places (never shuffled): a first step shows fire (A / Square), lightning (W / Triangle) and ice (D / Circle); the key picks it, then the usual key sequence and gesture follow. Also from the owner the same day: menus play a transition when their look changes, every skill point asks for confirmation, and the weapon tree is a hub with gun pages (v0.39 to v0.42).

- v0.42 (2026-11-13): owner chose three perk changes the architect proposed from the balance table: the pistol's Steady Grip becomes **Quick Draw** (aim 20% faster and move 10% faster while aiming, per rank), the shotgun's Steady Grip becomes **Extended Tube** (more shells), and the rifle gets **Extended Mag** (+5 rounds per magazine per rank). Measuring them showed that a bigger magazine also carries more ammo (spare magazines hold the bigger magazine; the shotgun's reserve is magazines x tube size), so the architect set Extended Tube to **+1 shell per rank** instead of the +2 shown to the owner: +2 doubled the shells carried, twice any other perk. Details in §18 "Weapon tree".

- **Jumps commit to their direction (owner, 2026-11-12):** like a real jump, the direction cannot be changed in the air (air control 0; the same when walking off a ledge). The direction is chosen at takeoff: the movement keys held at that moment. The second jump can choose a new direction and then commits again. Provisional details (architect): a jump from standing with a direction held leaves at 60% of walking speed at least; the second jump with a direction held leaves at walking speed at least, and with no direction held it keeps the current drift. The dash still works in the air and is not affected.

-- **Ledge climb (owner, 2026-11-13; details provisional, architect):** the player climbs onto a structure in two cases. (1) **In the air**, rising or falling, when the view faces a wall (within 60° of straight at it), the wall is right in front, and its top is between 15 cm and 1.6 m above the feet (the hands' reach): the climb starts on its own. (2) **Jump pressed on the ground** right against a wall the view faces, whose top is between 0.5 m and one jump's rise plus the 1.6 m reach above the feet: the climb starts instead of the jump; a higher wall is a normal jump (and the double jump can still reach a climb in the air). There must be room for the player on top and above the head. The climb rises straight up, then moves forward onto the top, in 0.22 s plus 0.18 s per metre of rise; it cannot be steered and blocks attacks, spells, dash and jump while it lasts (looking stays free). Enemies are never climbed. The first-person animation: the held item (staff, sword, gun) drops out of view, both pixel hands come up from the bottom of the screen with their sleeves and grip the ledge where it is on screen, the camera pulls down a little and dips 10° (with a slight roll) as it goes over the edge, then the hands let go and the held item comes back. Numbers in `Player.json` (`Mantle*`). Side effect handled in the test arena: the reach makes things higher reachable, so the last course step now needs the double jump even with a climb, the outer walls went from 11 m to 14 m, and the arena warns if the future-only platform (6 m) could be climbed in the past.

+- **Ledge climb (owner, 2026-11-13; details provisional, architect):** the player climbs onto a structure in two cases. (1) **In the air**, rising or falling, when a wall is right next to the player in the jump's direction (or anywhere around, if the jump is nearly vertical or was stopped by the wall), and its top is between 15 cm and 1.6 m above the feet (the hands' reach): the climb starts on its own. (2) **Jump pressed on the ground** right against a wall in the held movement direction (or anywhere around when no direction is held: back to the wall works; holding a direction away from a wall behind is a normal jump), whose top is between 0.5 m and one jump's rise plus the 1.6 m reach above the feet: the climb starts instead of the jump; a higher wall is a normal jump (and the double jump can still reach a climb in the air). The wall must be met roughly head-on (within 60° of its face). The view no longer has to face it (owner, v0.45): if the wall is more than 60° off the view, the view turns to face it during the rise, so the player ends on top looking across it; the mouse still works during the turn. There must be room for the player on top and above the head, and floor under the landing point. The climb rises straight up, then moves forward onto the top, in 0.22 s plus 0.18 s per metre of rise; it cannot be steered and blocks attacks, spells, dash and jump while it lasts (looking stays free). Enemies are never climbed. The first-person animation: the held item (staff, sword, gun) drops out of view, both pixel hands come up from the bottom of the screen with their sleeves and grip the ledge where it is on screen, the camera pulls down a little and dips 10° (with a slight roll) as it goes over the edge, then the hands let go and the held item comes back. Numbers in `Player.json` (`Mantle*`). Side effect handled in the test arena: the reach makes things higher reachable, so the last course step now needs the double jump even with a climb, the outer walls went from 11 m to 14 m, and the arena warns if the future-only platform (6 m) could be climbed in the past.

- **Double jump on day 1:** the player starts knowing the air passive "Double jump" so it can be tested now. In the real game it is learned in the air zone (§6); remove it from `Player.json` `StartingSpells` then.

- **Dash:** available from the start (the air passive only improves it). It goes in the movement direction (forward when standing still), works in the air, gives no invulnerability, and does not refill jumps.

- **Owning weapons:** decided by the owner for staffs (section 8): picked-up weapons go to the inventory and are equipped by hand. Provisional part: guns and the sword follow the same rule; each owned gun keeps its own ammo while stored.

Escalar de espaldas está en marcha: Muse lo está programando ahora y todavía no hay nada compilado ni subido.

**Cómo funcionará:** ya no importa hacia dónde mires. Para elegir el muro, el juego se fija en lo que quiere hacer el jugador:
- **En el suelo, sin pulsar dirección:** busca muro alrededor en las 8 direcciones, empezando por la que estás mirando. De espaldas a un bloque, pulsas salto y lo escalas.
- **En el suelo, pulsando una dirección:** solo se escala lo que hay en esa dirección. Si pulsas S hacia un muro que tienes detrás, lo escalas. Si pulsas W para alejarte de un muro que tienes detrás, haces un salto normal hacia delante, nunca un escalado hacia atrás.
- **En el aire:** cuenta la dirección del salto. Si el salto es casi vertical, o si chocaste con el muro y te frenó, busca alrededor. Así funciona saltar de espaldas pegado a una pared.
- **La cámara gira:** si el muro está a más de 60° de donde miras, la vista gira hacia él mientras subes y terminas arriba mirando hacia delante. El ratón sigue funcionando durante el giro.

Lo he dejado provisional: lo de "nunca escalar hacia atrás si pulsas en otra dirección" y el giro de cámara son decisiones mías. Ya están en el GDD (v0.45).

Cuando Muse termine: pruebas automáticas (de espaldas al muro de 2 m, de espaldas en el aire junto a la plataforma, y pulsando W lejos de un muro), revisión de Sol 6.1, verificación completa, y commit y push.

## Files changed
- `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Player/GBMantle.h/.cpp` — new pure `GetProbeDirections` (intent → that single normalized direction; no intent → 8 unit directions 45° apart starting with the view: 0, +45, −45, +90, −90, +135, −135, 180, CCW positive) with inline-allocator `TArray` (no heap, tick-safe); new pure `TurnFraction` (smoothstep 0→1 over Alpha 0→RiseShare, 1 after).
- `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Player/GBPlayerCharacter.h/.cpp` — `FindMantleLedge` now takes a probe direction and checks `dot(ProbeDir, −WallNormal2D) >= MantleApproachMinDot`; `TryStartMantle` builds the intent (ground: held-input world direction; air: horizontal velocity if ≥ `MantleAirSearchMinSpeed`) and tries directions in order, keeping the `Approach >= −50` check per found wall; air tick now goes through `TryStartMantle(false)`; `StartMantle` computes the signed shortest yaw turn when it exceeds `MantleTurnMinAngle`, `TickMantle` applies it in `TurnFraction` deltas (mouse still works, pitch untouched), `CancelMantle`/finish reset it; new `SetMoveInputForTest` smoke hook.
- `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Core/GBStatNames.h`, `Glyphbound/Content/Data/Player.json` — renamed `MantleFacingMinDot` → `MantleApproachMinDot` (0.5), added `MantleAirSearchMinSpeed` (150) and `MantleTurnMinAngle` (60).
- `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Tests/GBPlayerTests.cpp` — new `Glyphbound.Player.MantleProbe` (intent single/normalized, 8-dir shape/order, rotation with view, `TurnFraction` shape/monotonicity/RiseShare dependence).
- `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/Core/GBDevCommands.cpp` — 4 new `mantle:` steps before "back to the arena start" (back standing press, back result, back air grab + result, held-away-is-a-jump); arena-start shifted to M+6.5, `quit` to U+43.5.

  - `SMOKE mantle back air feet=602 x=1848 mantling=0 walking=1 yaw=0`
  - `SMOKE mantle held away mantling=0`
  - `SMOKE DONE`

Not committed, per instructions.

## Second round: climbing in any direction (GDD v0.45)
After the package, the owner wrote, in Spanish:

> *"Implementa que se pueda escalar sin mirar el muro, estando de espalda por ejemplo."*

Translation: "Make it possible to climb without looking at the wall, with your back to it, for example."

**Design (architect, provisional).** The view no longer picks the wall. The player's intent does:
- **On the ground:** the held movement direction. With no direction held, the climb looks all around in 8 directions, the view's first, then +-45, +-90, +-135 and 180 degrees. So with your back to a wall and no keys held, a jump press climbs it. Holding S into a wall behind you climbs it. Holding W away from a wall behind you is a normal jump forward, never a climb backwards.
- **In the air:** the jump's own direction (jumps commit to it). When the horizontal speed is under 1.5 m/s (a vertical jump, or a jump the wall has stopped), the climb looks all around.
- **The view turns.** When the wall is more than 60 degrees off the view, the view turns to it during the rise, so the player ends on top looking across. The turn is applied in deltas, so the mouse keeps working during it.
- Stats: `MantleFacingMinDot` became `MantleApproachMinDot` (the probe has to meet the wall within 60 degrees of its face). New: `MantleAirSearchMinSpeed` (150) and `MantleTurnMinAngle` (60).

**Build.**
- Brief `Prompts/mantle_any_direction.md`, implemented by **Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor (High)** via OpenCode (default implementer).
- New pure functions `GBMantle::GetProbeDirections` and `TurnFraction`, test `Glyphbound.Player.MantleProbe`, and four new `mantle:` smoke steps: back to the 2 m wall, back to the platform in the air, and holding away from a wall behind.

**Review: GPT Sol 6.1** (run `203639-codex-a57072`, prompt `Prompts/mantle_any_direction_review_sol.md`). Four findings, all fixed by the architect (small, already diagnosed):
- **P2, a real input-order bug:** Enhanced Input fires the jump's `Started` before the same frame's `Move` event. So pressing W and jump together with your back to a wall read "no direction held" and would climb backwards. The climb now reads the Move action's current value (`UEnhancedPlayerInput::GetActionValue`), not the last Move event.
- **P3:** the "held away" smoke step only checked "not climbing" right after the press. It now also checks, 0.2 simulated seconds later, a real jump: falling, rising and moving away from the wall. That follow-up check caught a gap in the smoke's own input hook: the hook fed the climb decision but not the jump's take-off direction. The jump left with no speed and grabbed the wall behind it in the air. In the game, a held W gives the jump its speed (450 cm/s) by take-off. The hook now feeds both.
- **P3:** the probe test now checks the full priority order, and the turn test checks smoothstep values at a quarter and three quarters of the rise (a linear turn would pass the old one).

**Known trade-off for the owner:** a vertical jump right next to a block taller than 0.5 m now climbs it even if the player is not looking at it. That is what was asked, but in combat it may happen by accident.
EOF
echo ok

- **On the ground:** the held movement direction. With no direction held, the climb looks all around in 8 directions, the view's first, then +-45, +-90, +-135 and 180 degrees. So with your back to a wall and no keys held, a jump press climbs it. Holding S into a wall behind you climbs it. Holding W away from a wall behind you is a normal jump forward, never a climb backwards.
- **In the air:** the jump's own direction (jumps commit to it). When the horizontal speed is under 1.5 m/s (a vertical jump, or a jump the wall has stopped), the climb looks all around.
- **The view turns.** When the wall is more than 60 degrees off the view, the view turns to it during the rise, so the player ends on top looking across. The turn is applied in deltas, so the mouse keeps working during it.
- Stats: `MantleFacingMinDot` became `MantleApproachMinDot` (the probe has to meet the wall within 60 degrees of its face). New: `MantleAirSearchMinSpeed` (150) and `MantleTurnMinAngle` (60).

**Build.**
- Brief `Prompts/mantle_any_direction.md`, implemented by **Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor (High)** via OpenCode (default implementer).
- New pure functions `GBMantle::GetProbeDirections` and `TurnFraction`, test `Glyphbound.Player.MantleProbe`, and four new `mantle:` smoke steps: back to the 2 m wall, back to the platform in the air, and holding away from a wall behind.

**Review: GPT Sol 6.1** (run `203639-codex-a57072`, prompt `Prompts/mantle_any_direction_review_sol.md`). Four findings, all fixed by the architect (small, already diagnosed):
- **P2, a real input-order bug:** Enhanced Input fires the jump's `Started` before the same frame's `Move` event. So pressing W and jump together with your back to a wall read "no direction held" and would climb backwards. The climb now reads the Move action's current value (`UEnhancedPlayerInput::GetActionValue`), not the last Move event.
- **P3:** the "held away" smoke step only checked "not climbing" right after the press. It now also checks, 0.2 simulated seconds later, a real jump: falling, rising and moving away from the wall. That follow-up check caught a gap in the smoke's own input hook: the hook fed the climb decision but not the jump's take-off direction. The jump left with no speed and grabbed the wall behind it in the air. In the game, a held W gives the jump its speed (450 cm/s) by take-off. The hook now feeds both.
- **P3:** the probe test now checks the full priority order, and the turn test checks smoothstep values at a quarter and three quarters of the rise (a linear turn would pass the old one).

**Known trade-off for the owner:** a vertical jump right next to a block taller than 0.5 m now climbs it even if the player is not looking at it. That is what was asked, but in combat it may happen by accident.
EOF

Escalar de espaldas ya pasa las pruebas filtradas. Ahora corre la verificación completa (build del juego, todos los tests y el smoke entero); cuando termine hago commit y push.

**Lo que encontró Sol y quedó arreglado:**
- **Un fallo real:** si pulsabas W y salto a la vez, de espaldas a un muro, el juego procesaba el salto antes que el movimiento. Creía que no había dirección y escalaba hacia atrás. Ahora lee la dirección pulsada en ese mismo momento.
- **El smoke no comprobaba un salto de verdad.** Al endurecerlo salió que la herramienta de prueba no le pasaba la dirección al salto. Ya está corregida: pulsando hacia delante lejos de un muro sale un salto normal a 450 cm/s alejándose, sin escalar.
- **Tests más estrictos:** ahora comprueban el orden exacto en que se buscan las direcciones y que el giro de la vista sea suave al empezar y al terminar.

**Un efecto que conviene valorar al jugar:** saltar en el sitio pegado a cualquier bloque lo escala, aunque no lo mires.
- Desde 50 cm de alto, escala nada más pulsar salto.
- Con bloques más bajos (de 15 a 50 cm), se agarra ya en el aire.

Es lo que pediste, pero en combate podría pasar sin querer. Si molesta, se puede limitar la búsqueda en el aire a bloques más altos.

Todo queda anotado en el GDD (v0.45) y en la bitácora.
